Best Ball, Ep. 2: Our Epic Ireland Golf Trip With Jordan Spieth's victory at the 2017 British Open Championship, he has three legs of the career Grand Slam in golf (2015 Masters, 2015 US Open, 2017 British Open Championship), making him one of the youngest golfers in history to three majors and three legs of the Grand Slam. Spieth now is able to complete the career Grand Slam with a win in the PGA Championship, which is played in 2026 at Aronimink Golf Club in Newtown Square, Pennsylvania, and has been the home of the BMW Championship on the PGA Tour. Spieth is currenlty one of three active golfers who can complete the career Grand Slam. The others are Phil Mickelson and Scottie Scheffler. Phil Mickelson needs to win the US Open to take the career Grand Slam after winning the 2004 Masters, 2005 PGA Championship and 2013 British Open Championship. Scheffler also needs to win the US Open after winning the 2022 Masters for his first major, then the PGA Championship and Open Championship in 2025. Rory McIlroy is the most recent player to complete the career Grand Slam after won the 2025 Masters, following winning the 2011 US Open, 2012 PGA Championship and 2014 British Open Championship. LISTEN TO GOLF NEWS NET RADIO 24/7 FOLLOW GOLF NEWS NET RADIO: iHEART | TUNEIN Only six golfers have ever captured the career Grand Slam: Rory McIlroy, Tiger Woods, Jack Nicklaus, Gary Player, Ben Hogan and Gene Sarazen. Bobby Jones won what was then known as the Grand Slam, including two amateur events and the two Opens. Events reflect first career Grand Slam Rory McIlroy: 2011 US Open, 2012 PGA Championship, 2014 British Open Championship, 2025 Masters Tiger Woods: 1997 Masters, 2000 US Open, 2000 Open Championship, 2000 PGA Championship Jack Nicklaus: 1962 US Open, 1963 Masters, 1963 PGA Championship, 1966 Open Championship Gary Player: 1959 Open Championship, 1961 Masters, 1962 PGA Championship, 1965 US Open Ben Hogan: 1946 PGA Championship, 1948 US Open, 1951 Masters, 1953 Open Championship Gene Sarazen: 1922 US Open, 1922 PGA Championship, 1932 Open Championship, 1935 Masters
